question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Sei Shōnagon's Pillow Book contains a list called "Things That Are Unpleasant to See," in which the author complains about grimy carriage windows, hurried walking, and collars that have been pulled back. Recorded with a sharp yet plain eye by Shōnagon—who served as a lady-in-waiting to Empress Teishi in the tenth century—such lists ______ the small everyday details of courtly life in Japan.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The plural subject 'such lists' requires the plural verb 'reveal.'

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? The word "karst"—which names a limestone landscape pocked with caves and sinkholes—is the subject of an essay by Barbara ______ in Barry Lopez and Debra Gwartney's Home Ground: A Guide to the American Landscape, the essay helps demonstrate the rich vocabulary North Americans have for describing terrain.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A period after 'Kingsolver' correctly separates two independent clauses.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? In 2022, Kevin Del Águila, a researcher who works with environmental DNA, took part in a 38-day expedition to Alto Mayo, a densely settled region in northern Peru. Scientists had long presumed that areas with dense human populations were improbable places to discover new species. Even so, Del Águila and his fellow team members ______ for such species in Alto Mayo found 27 of them, among them 3 amphibian species new to science.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The participle 'searching' modifies the subject that performs the main verb 'found.'

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? To grasp what scholars believe to be the allegorical intent of Gentileschi's 17th-century painting ______ to embody the power female artists wield in the visual arts—a viewer must become acquainted with the work's symbolic elements.
subject: Reading and Writing

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? In 2022, Carnegie Hall's digital Timeline of African American Music was ______ input from George Starks, Maureen Mahon, and other leading scholars--to combine text with music clips, so that users could both read about and directly experience genres such as bebop and gospel.
subject: Reading and Writing

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? In 1813, the French paleontologist Georges Cuvier suggested that catastrophic events are responsible for shaping Earth's geologic features. This theory ______ to account for geological evolution, though it enjoyed wide acceptance for a time, ultimately fell out of favor within the scientific community.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The participle 'attempting' modifies the subject 'theory,' whose main verb is 'fell out of favor.'

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Under the Hornbostel-Sachs system, musical instruments are grouped according to the way they generate sound. The đàn bầu, for instance—a widely played Vietnamese instrument—produces sound chiefly through the vibration of its strings. ______ within the Hornbostel-Sachs framework, the đàn bầu counts as a chordophone.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Thus' signals the conclusion drawn from the instrument's string-based sound production.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Were you able to fly a spaceship to Carpo, one of Jupiter's many moons, you'd encounter a moon whose orbit is prograde—meaning Carpo circles Jupiter in the very direction the planet spins on its axis. ______ at Herse, another of Jupiter's moons, you'd come across a retrograde orbit, in which the moon travels around Jupiter in the opposite direction.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Elsewhere' contrasts the prograde orbit at Carpo with the retrograde orbit at Herse.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Basic as the question might appear, biologists have not reached agreement on what a species actually is: some endorse the genetic species concept (Baker and Bradley 2006), whereas others follow the Darwinian species concept (Jolly 2014). ______ proponents of a pluralist approach--rather than a single, monistic concept-- contend that a range of species concepts suits the equally varied ways the term is applied across the field.
option a: However, some scholars posit that, outside the human desire to name things, species don't exist;
option b: Counterintuitively, this lack of agreement may not be without its virtues;
option c: Accordingly, many biologists seek to find a universal species concept;
option d: Indeed, this definitional stalemate is widely known as the species problem;
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Counterintuitively' fits the idea that the lack of consensus may actually be beneficial.

question: Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to emphasize a similarity between the two sculptures? While researching, a student has noted the following: Richard Serra was an American artist celebrated for his large metal sculptures. One of them, Rounds: Equal Weight, Unequal Measure, is made of weathering steel and measures 17 feet wide and 7 feet tall. Another, Circuit, is made of hot-rolled steel and measures 24 feet wide and 1 foot tall.
option a: Circuit is one of artist Richard Serra's large metal sculptures.
option b: Rounds: Equal Weight, Unequal Measure and Circuit are both large metal sculptures by artist Richard Serra.
option c: Richard Serra's Rounds: Equal Weight, Unequal Measure is 17 feet wide and 7 feet tall.
option d: Rounds: Equal Weight, Unequal Measure is made from a different kind of steel than Circuit.

question: Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to emphasize when Makeba became popular? A student has gathered these notes: Miriam Makeba, a South African singer, became famous during the 1960s for her jazz-tinged versions of traditional Xhosa songs. Her 1960 album Miriam Makeba includes the Xhosa song "Olilili." She also earned recognition for covering many well-known European and American songs, among them "For What It's Worth," which the American rock band Buffalo Springfield first made popular; Makeba's rendition appears on her 1970 album Keep Me in Mind.
option a: The song "Olilili" appears on Miriam Makeba's album Miriam Makeba, which she released in 1960.
option b: Originally made popular by Buffalo Springfield, the song "For What It's Worth" appears on Miriam Makeba's 1970 album Keep Me in Mind.
option c: The songs "Olilili" and "For What It's Worth" can both be found on albums recorded by the South African singer Miriam Makeba.
option d: Known for her renditions of both traditional Xhosa songs and songs made popular by European and American artists, South African singer Miriam Makeba rose to fame in the 1960s.

shortexplanation: Choice D foregrounds that Makeba rose to fame in the 1960s.

question: Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to emphasize how long Lauren Woolstencroft competed in the Paralympic Games? A student has assembled these notes: The Paralympic Games are a set of international athletic competitions for athletes who have an impairment, and a gold medal signals a first-place finish. As a Paralympic swimmer, Priya Cooper competed from 1992 to 2000, earning twenty-four medals, fifteen of them gold. As a Paralympic alpine skier, Lauren Woolstencroft competed from 2002 to 2010, earning ten medals, eight of them gold.
option a: Swimmer Priya Cooper made her Paralympic debut in 1992, while alpine skier Lauren Woolstencroft made her debut in 2002.
option b: An accomplished Paralympian with multiple gold medal wins, Lauren Woolstencroft competed as an alpine skier from 2002 to 2010.
option c: Alpine skiing, a sport in which Lauren Woolstencroft took home eight gold medals, has been an event at the Paralympic Games since 1976.
option d: During her career as a Paralympic alpine skier, Lauren Woolstencroft took home a total of ten medals, eight of which were gold.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Choice B highlights the 2002-to-2010 span of Woolstencroft's competition.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Scleractinian corals—the stony kinds, such as lettuce leaf corals and rice corals—act as habitat builders and form the base of coral reef ecosystems, with a single reef usually being constructed by several species at once. A reef's ______ depends heavily on this redundancy, since having multiple species lowers the chance that a crucial function will cease if any one species falls prey to a vulnerability.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Resiliency' captures a reef's ability to withstand the loss of one of its species.

question: Assuming the data in the table are broadly representative, do the data support the researcher's hypothesis as presented in the text? Average Frontation Angle for Five Species, by Family, Habitat, and Preferred Substrate — Species / Family / Habitat / Preferred substrate / Frontation angle (°): Vulpes lagopus, Canidae, open, terrestrial, 54.89; Nyctereutes procyonoides, Canidae, closed, arboreal, 56.51; Lynx lynx, Felidae, closed, terrestrial, 65.67; Leptailurus serval, Felidae, open, terrestrial, 65.80; Leopardus wiedii, Felidae, closed, arboreal, 67.61. By tracking how traits are distributed across phylogenetic lineages, evolutionary biologists can tell whether shared traits arise from common ancestry—so that closely related species reliably display the trait—or from convergent evolution under comparable selective pressures, in which case the trait appears independently in more distantly related species that occupy similar ecological niches. Suspecting that the orientation of the orbit (eye socket) in the families Canidae and Felidae—both within the order Carnivora—stems chiefly from the latter process, a researcher measured frontation angles, meaning how far the orbits tilt downward or upward, in felid and canid species living in different habitats and favoring different substrates.
option a: No, because frontation angles are relatively consistent across ecological categories, with values for species inhabiting closed arboreal habitats and species inhabiting open terrestrial habitats ranging from 56.51 to 67.61 and from 54.89 to 65.80, respectively
option b: Yes, because frontation angles show a moderately strong relationship with ecological niches, with two out of the three species with the highest frontation angles either inhabiting closed habitats or preferring terrestrial substrates
option c: No, because frontation angles cluster by taxonomic family rather than by ecological categories, with similar values measured for species from the same family despite their occupation of different ecological niches
option d: Yes, because frontation angles are lower for canid species than for felid species regardless of habitat or preferred substrate, with values for species from the same taxonomic family clustering in a relatively narrow range
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Angles cluster by family rather than ecological niche, so the data do not support the hypothesis.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Seeking to address Sumitava Mukherjee et al.'s claim that low financial stakes weaken loss aversion--the tendency to feel losses more sharply than equal gains--and thereby to test an idea that has shaped research from behavioral economics to transportation studies, Kellen Mrvka et al. ran a study in which certain participants encountered scenarios involving ______ amounts of money.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? The Heege Manuscript (HM) is made up of assorted texts that Richard Heege copied out at his home in fifteenth-century England. question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
